item.title: Re: New fairer voting system
item.content:encoded:
Talked this over with other staff for a bit and we're not interested in implementing this idea, since it would be rather disruptive to the reading experience and not really possible given Wikidot's infrastructure. Voting as it exists now is a very passive and reader-driven experience, almost an afterthought, so most people probably aren't going to be on board for making it a more active and structured system.

Moreover, while Wikidot can handle randomness somewhat, it's rather finicky and there's not really a way to weight probability based on vote count. There just isn't a reasonable way to implement what you're describing.

… while dramatically good new articles can't ever hope to catch up over time due to the very existence of the "http://www.scpwiki.com/top-rated-pages" page unless the reader really wants to read more than 1000 articles.

Top Rated Pages isn't generally how people discover popular articles; most of those are rated so high because they have some presence outside of the community on Reddit, YouTube, etc., or they were written by a popular author, or any other number of reasons. While the goal of promoting newer works is admirable, this solution wouldn't be particularly effective in curtailing that behavior.

item.title: New fairer voting system
item.content:encoded:
I feel a NEW voting system based on upvotes-per-view would stop good and nostalgic but not awesome ancient articles from being so very dramatically advantaged on top lists, while dramatically good new articles can't ever hope to catch up over time due to the very existence of the "http://www.scpwiki.com/top-rated-pages" page unless the reader really wants to read more than 1000 articles.

We need a system like this one.
http://www.kittenwar.com/
You can tell the "losingest" kittens are not there just because they are new, and the "winningest" kittens aren't there because they are old, this system does a better job of ranking quality than the current system.

The system would require:
-Knowing which SCP numbers are not a 404 or empty page or administrative issues page.

-The reader is shown 2 article links, they open in a new tabs. The first is fully random (to be fair), and the other is bias toward articles that showed up less in the NEW voting system 20 percent of the time, and fully random the rest of the time.

-The reader is asked after reading both articles to return to the tab of origin and pick which one they prefer.

-The best articles will win more "SCPfights".

-If you don't do it, some extrernal site will and will have ads on top of the "rate my SCP!" voting thingy.

Thoughts?
